provenance.method: lesson notes written from the NERDC 2025 scheme of work outline; every week keeps its scheme topic and bullets as the teaching spine

topics.title: Money 1
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to identify naira coins and notes.
The pupils should be able to recognize 5, 10, 20, 50 naira.

Introduction:
Today we learn about money.
Money is what we use to buy things.

Content:
Money is naira in Nigeria.
We have coins and notes.
Look at the 5 naira coin.
It is small and brown.
Look at the 10 naira note.
It is green.
Show me the 20 naira note.
Point to the 50 naira coin.

Class activity:
Let's play money sorting.
Each pupil gets play money.
Sort coins and notes on your table.

Evaluation questions:
What is money used for?
Show me a 10 naira note.
Which is bigger 20 or 50 naira?
How many 5 naira make 10 naira?

Summary:
Today we learned about naira coins and notes.

topics.title: Money 2
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to buy and sell in a play market.
The pupils should be able to add simple prices and pay correctly.

Introduction:
Last week we learned about naira.
Today we use money to buy things.

Content:
In the market we buy and sell.
Price is how much something costs.
If a pencil is 10 naira and a book is 20 naira.
Together they cost 30 naira.
Count your money before you pay.
Give the correct amount to the seller.

Class activity:
We make a class market.
Some pupils are sellers.
Some pupils are buyers.
Use play money to buy things.

Evaluation questions:
What do we use to pay in the market?
If a banana costs 5 naira how much for two?
What do we do before we pay money?

Summary:
Today we bought and sold things using money.

topics.title: Time 1
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to tell o'clock time on a clock face.
The pupils should be able to make a paper clock.

Introduction:
We use clocks to tell time.
Time helps us know when things happen.

Content:
A clock has numbers and hands.
The long hand points to 12 for o'clock.
The short hand points to the hour.
When short hand points to 3 it is 3 o'clock.
When short hand points to 8 it is 8 o'clock.

Class activity:
Each pupil makes a paper clock.
Draw numbers 1 to 12 on the clock face.
Cut out clock hands with paper.
Attach hands with a split pin.
Move the hands to show o'clock time.

Evaluation questions:
What does the long hand show at o'clock?
Show me 2 o'clock on your clock.
What time does school start?

Summary:
We learned to tell o'clock time on a clock.

topics.title: Time 2
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to tell half past time.
The pupils should be able to make a daily time table.

Introduction:
Last week we learned o'clock time.
Today we learn half past time.

Content:
Half past is between hours.
The long hand points to 6 for half past.
The short hand is between two numbers.
For half past 2 the short hand is between 2 and 3.
School starts at 8 o'clock in the morning.
We eat lunch at 12 o'clock.

Class activity:
Let's make a daily time table.
Draw pictures of school activities.
Write time under each picture.
For example 8 o'clock - school bell.

Evaluation questions:
Where does the long hand point at half past?
Show me half past 5 on your clock.
What time do we eat lunch?

Summary:
We learned half past time and made our time table.

topics.title: Length
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to compare longer and shorter objects.
The pupils should be able to measure using hand spans.

Introduction:
Some things are long.
Some things are short.

Content:
Length means how long something is.
We can compare with our eyes.
A pencil is shorter than a ruler.
We can measure with hand spans.
One hand span is from your thumb to little finger.
Use the same hand to measure everything.

Class activity:
Let's measure our desks.
Each pupil measures with hand spans.
Count how many hand spans long your desk is.
Compare with your friend's desk.

Evaluation questions:
Which is longer a book or a pencil?
How many hand spans is your table?
What can we use to measure length?

Summary:
We learned about longer and shorter things.

topics.title: Weight
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to compare heavy and light objects.
The pupils should be able to use a pan balance to weigh.

Introduction:
Some things are heavy to carry.
Some things are light to carry.

Content:
Weight means how heavy something is.
A stone is heavy.
A feather is light.
We use a pan balance to compare weight.
Put objects on both sides.
The side that goes down is heavier.
The side that goes up is lighter.

Class activity:
Let's weigh fruits and blocks.
Place a fruit on one side of the balance.
Add blocks to the other side until it balances.
Count how many blocks equal the fruit.

Evaluation questions:
Which is heavier a book or a feather?
What does the pan balance show us?
How do we know which object is heavier?

Summary:
We learned about heavy and light things.

topics.title: Capacity
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to identify full, half full and empty containers.
The pupils should be able to measure capacity with water play.

Introduction:
Capacity is how much a container can hold.
Some containers hold more than others.

Content:
Full means no more can fit.
Empty means there is nothing inside.
Half full means it is half way.
We can use cups to measure.
One cup fills a small jug twice.
The jug has double capacity of the cup.

Class activity:
Let's do water measuring.
Each pupil gets different cups and jugs.
Fill cups with water from the basin.
Pour water into jugs to see how many cups fill them.
Mark full, half and empty on your jugs.

Evaluation questions:
What does full mean?
Show me a half full cup.
Which holds more a cup or a jug?

Summary:
We learned about full, half full and empty containers.

topics.title: Data fun
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to count and mark their favorites.
The pupils should be able to make a pictograph of favorite fruits.

Introduction:
We can collect information about things.
Information helps us see what is popular.

Content:
Data is information we collect.
We can count how many like something.
A pictograph uses pictures to show data.
Each picture stands for one thing.
If we count fruits we draw pictures of fruits.
More pictures mean more people like it.

Class activity:
Let's make a fruit pictograph.
Each pupil chooses their favorite fruit.
Draw the fruit on a card.
Stick cards on the board in rows.
Count how many for each fruit.

Evaluation questions:
What is data?
What does each picture show in a pictograph?
Which fruit has the most pictures?

Summary:
We made a pictograph with our favorite fruits.

topics.title: Halves first step
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to identify half of shapes and objects.
The pupils should be able to fold and shade half of a shape.

Introduction:
Today we learn about halves.
Half means two equal parts.

Content:
When we cut something in half we get two equal parts.
Each part is one half.
A circle folded in half makes two semicircles.
A square folded in half makes two rectangles.
Half of 10 is 5.
Half of 8 is 4.

Class activity:
Let's fold and shade shapes.
Each pupil gets paper shapes.
Fold each shape exactly in half.
Open the fold and shade one half.

Evaluation questions:
What does half mean?
Show me half of this circle.
What is half of 6?

Summary:
We learned about halves and how to find them.

topics.title: Revision and maths market day
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to participate in a class market.
The pupils should be able to measure and weigh at stations.

Introduction:
Today we revise what we learned.
We will have a maths market day.

Content:
We use money to buy and sell.
We tell time on clocks.
We measure length and weight.
 We find halves of things.
At the market we use all these skills.
Each station has a different activity.

Class activity:
We run a class market with stations.
Money station: buy things with naira notes.
Time station: show o'clock and half past time.
Measure station: measure length with hand spans.
Weight station: compare heavy and light objects.
Half station: fold papers to show halves.

Evaluation questions:
What did you buy at the market?
How did you measure at the station?
What time did you show at the time station?

Summary:
We had fun revising maths at our market day.
